lessons.title: Views and modifiers
lessons.body: A SwiftUI view is a lightweight struct that describes a piece of UI. Each modifier wraps the view in a new view, so the order you apply them in changes the result.
keyPoints: Views are value types, cheap to create and recreate
Each modifier returns a new view that wraps the old one
Order matters: padding then background differs from background then padding

lessons.title: Stacks and layout
lessons.body: HStack, VStack and ZStack arrange their children. Spacer and frame decide how the free space is shared. ViewThatFits picks the first layout that fits the space offered.
keyPoints: A parent proposes a size and each child chooses its own
Spacer expands to fill the free space along the stack's axis
ViewThatFits uses the first child that fits

lessons.title: State and Binding
lessons.body: @State gives a view its own source of truth. @Binding lets a child read and write state that its parent owns.
keyPoints: @State is owned by the view and survives re-renders
$value passes a Binding, a read-write reference to that state
Keep one source of truth: children get bindings, not copies

lessons.title: Lists and identity
lessons.body: List and ForEach build rows from a collection. Each element needs a stable identity so SwiftUI can match rows between updates.
keyPoints: Identifiable gives each element a stable id
Stable ids keep row state and animations correct
Never use array indices or fresh UUIDs as ids for changing data

lessons.title: Navigation
lessons.body: NavigationStack pushes screens by value. A NavigationLink appends a value, and navigationDestination says which view shows it.
keyPoints: Push by value instead of building the destination inline
Values you push must be Hashable
A path you own makes deep links and state restoration possible

lessons.title: Codable and bundle data
lessons.body: Codable turns JSON into Swift types. This app ships its lessons inside the bundle as lessons.json and decodes them at launch.
keyPoints: Codable is synthesized when every stored property is Codable
JSON keys must match property names unless you add CodingKeys
A DecodingError's codingPath points at the bad field

lessons.title: Previews and assets
lessons.body: #Preview renders a view in Xcode without running the app. The asset catalog holds colors and images with light and dark variants.
keyPoints: Previews need sample data, so keep Lesson.sample handy
Check dark mode and large text in previews, not only on a device
Asset catalog colors switch automatically between light and dark
